questions.q: What is Arkwright chiefly credited with?
options: Inventing the spinning jenny that let one worker run many spindles
Building the factory system that combined power, machinery and labour for mass yarn
Founding Britain's cotton trade by importing raw cotton from India
Inventing the steam engine that powered the first Lancashire mills
questions.explain: He combined power, machinery, semi-skilled labour and cotton, earning the title father of the modern factory system.

questions.q: What did Arkwright invent while working as a barber and wig-maker, which funded his machinery?
options: A cheaper fabric for making wigs
questions.explain: He invented a waterproof dye for periwigs whose income later funded his prototype cotton machinery.

questions.q: When was the world's first water-powered mill built at Cromford?
questions.explain: In 1771 the partners built the world's first water-powered mill at Cromford.

questions.q: What were the Cromford shift arrangements?
options: Two 13-hour shifts a day; latecomers lost an extra day's pay
Three 8-hour shifts a day, with bells at 6 am, 2 pm and 10 pm
Two 10-hour shifts a day, with no holidays for workers
One 12-hour day shift; latecomers were docked an hour's pay
questions.explain: Work ran in two 13-hour shifts; gates shut at 6, and latecomers lost the day and an extra day's pay.

questions.q: What does the passage suggest about Arkwright's grand patent?
options: The court upheld it in 1785, confirming Arkwright's monopoly over cotton spinning machinery
Public opinion strongly backed exclusive patents, so his case succeeded quickly
Lewis Paul's heirs won control of the patent after suing Arkwright in the 1780s
His case failed partly because of deficient specifications and doubts he invented the frame
questions.explain: The case was settled against him because his specifications were deficient and others were said to be the inventor.
